section.heading: Emergency entry to premises without warrant—post-entry warrants

content.p: Requirement to apply for post-entry warrant
A police officer who has entered premises under, or purportedly under, subsection 3UEA(1) must:
(a) apply to an assessment officer for a warrant (a post-entry warrant) under this section in relation to the entry to the premises; and
do so as soon as practicable after the exercise, or purported exercise, of powers under section 3UEA in relation to the premises.
The application must:
be in writing; and
(b) set out:
the nature of the matters suspected by the police officer for the purposes of paragraphs 3UEA(1)(a) and (b); and
the grounds on which the police officer held the suspicion; and
state whether the police officer is:
(i) a member of the Australian Federal Police (within the meaning of the Australian Federal Police Act 1979); or
a special member (within the meaning of that Act); or
a member, however described, of a police force of a State or Territory; and
if the police officer is a member mentioned in subparagraph (c)(iii) of this subsection—identify the relevant State or Territory; and
state the police officer’s name, rank, identification number (however described) and police station (if applicable and necessary); and
(f) state the police officer’s contact details, including details of how the assessment officer may give to the police officer the following:
any request in writing under subsection (4) of this section for information or documents;
the post-entry warrant or a notice of refusal to issue the warrant; and

if the police officer is a member, or special member, mentioned in subparagraph (c)(i) or (ii) of this subsection—include details of how the assessment officer may give to the Commissioner the post-entry warrant or a notice of refusal to issue the warrant; and

if the police officer is a member mentioned in subparagraph (c)(iii) of this subsection—include details of how the assessment officer may give to the Commissioner of Police in the police force of the relevant State or Territory, or the person holding equivalent rank, the post-entry warrant or a notice of refusal to issue the warrant; and
set out any information that:
is known to the police officer; and

the police officer considers may assist the assessment officer to give, to any current or former owners or occupiers of the premises who have been affected by the exercise, or purported exercise, of the powers under section 3UEA in relation to the premises, the post-entry warrant or a notice of refusal to issue the warrant; and
set out the time, date and place of the entry; and
set out any other information, and be accompanied by any documents, the police officer considers relevant to the application.
The information in the application must be sworn or affirmed by the police officer.
Requesting further information or documents
The assessment officer may request, in writing, that the police officer provide further information or documents relating to the application, and that the police officer do so in a particular way.
If the police officer is unable to provide some or all of the further information or documents requested, the police officer must, within a reasonable period, notify the assessment officer:
of the information or documents that cannot be provided; and
of the reasons why the information or documents cannot be provided.

If the assessment officer is notified in accordance with subsection (5) that some or all of the further information or documents cannot be provided, the assessment officer must (unless there is another reason not to) continue to consider the application despite having not received the further information or documents.
Issue of warrant
The assessment officer must:

issue the post-entry warrant if, and only if, the assessment officer is satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that in entering the premises the police officer suspected, on reasonable grounds, the matters mentioned in paragraphs 3UEA(1)(a) and (b); and
otherwise, refuse to issue the post-entry warrant.
The issue of, or refusal to issue, the post-entry warrant does not affect whether or not the exercise, or purported exercise, of powers under section 3UEA was valid.

Note: Section 138 of the Evidence Act 1995 (discretion to exclude improperly or illegally obtained evidence) may apply to evidence obtained as a result of the exercise, or purported exercise, of powers under section 3UEA of this Act.
Content of warrant
The post-entry warrant, if issued, must include the following:
the information mentioned in paragraphs (2)(c), (d), (e) and (j);
a statement of the reasons for issuing the warrant;
a statement that the warrant has been issued under this section.
Notification requirements

If the assessment officer issues the post-entry warrant, the assessment officer must give a copy of the warrant to the persons mentioned in subsection (12) as soon as reasonably practicable after issuing the warrant.
If the assessment officer refuses to issue the post-entry warrant:
the assessment officer must give written notice of the refusal to the persons mentioned in subsection (12) as soon as reasonably practicable after refusing to issue the warrant; and
the notice must include a statement of reasons for refusing to issue the warrant; and
in the case of a notice given to a person mentioned in paragraph (12)(d)—the notice must also contain information about any right the person may have to:
(i) make a complaint to the Commonwealth Ombudsman under the Ombudsman Act 1976; or
take civil or other action;
in relation to the entry to the premises or the exercise, or purported exercise, of powers under section 3UEA in relation to the premises.
For the purposes of subsections (10) and (11), the persons are the following:
the police officer;

(b) if the police officer is a member of the Australian Federal Police (within the meaning of the Australian Federal Police Act 1979) or a special member (within the meaning of that Act)—the Commissioner;
if the police officer is a member, however described, of a police force of a State or Territory—the Commissioner of Police in that police force or the person holding equivalent rank;
any current or former owners or occupiers of the premises:
whom the assessment officer considers have been affected by the exercise, or purported exercise, of the powers under section 3UEA in relation to the premises; and
to whom the assessment officer considers it is practicable to give the post-entry warrant or notice of refusal (as the case requires).
Protection of information

(13) Despite subsections (9) and (11), a post-entry warrant or notice of refusal must not include information if disclosure of that information is likely to prejudice national security (within the meaning of the National Security Information (Criminal and Civil Proceedings) Act 2004).

section.heading: Conditions of an interim control order

content.p: General conditions
Without limiting the conditions that the issuing court may impose on the person by the order, those conditions may relate to any of the following:
that the person not be present at one or more of the following:
specified areas or places;
specified classes of areas or places;
any area or place determined by a specified authority;
that the person reside at specified premises, and not begin to reside at any other premises without the prior permission of a specified authority;
that the person remain at specified premises between specified times each day, or on specified days, subject to subsection (5);
that the person not leave Australia, or the State or Territory in which the person’s residence is located;
that the person provide a specified authority with the person’s passport (or passports) while the order is in force;
that the person not change the person’s name, or use any name that is not specified in the order;
that the person not apply for one or more of the following:
any Australian travel document;
any travel document of a foreign country;
any licence to operate equipment, machinery, a heavy vehicle or a weapon, or any licence to possess a weapon;
that the person not communicate or associate by any means (including through third parties) with one or more of the following:
specified individuals;
specified classes of individuals;
any individuals determined by a specified authority;
that the person not access or use specified forms of telecommunication or other technology (including the internet);
that the person not possess or use specified articles or substances;
that the person not carry out specified activities;
that the person not engage in one or more of the following:
specified work;
specified classes of work;
specified activities relating to specified work or classes of work;
that the person not engage in any training or education without the prior permission of a specified authority;
that the person do any or all of the following:
attend and participate in treatment, rehabilitation or intervention programs or activities;
undertake psychological or psychiatric assessment or counselling;
as specified in the order or as directed by a specified authority;
that the person attend and participate in interviews and assessments (including for the purposes of paragraph (n)) as specified in the order or as directed by a specified authority;
that the person allow the results of the interviews and assessments referred to in paragraph (o), and any other specified information, to be disclosed to a specified authority;
that the person provide specified information to a specified authority within a specified period or before a specified event;

that the person comply with any reasonable direction given to the person by a specified authority in relation to any specified condition (whether or not the condition is imposed in accordance with this subsection).
Note: See also subsections (9) and (10) and section 100.1 in relation to references to premises, reside or residence, and work.
Conditions relating to monitoring and enforcement
Without limiting the conditions that the issuing court may impose on the person by the order, those conditions may also relate to any of the following:
that the person submit to testing by a specified authority in relation to the possession or use of specified articles or substances;
that the person allow themselves to be photographed by a specified authority;
that the person allow impressions of the person’s fingerprints to be taken by a specified authority;

that the person be subject to electronic monitoring (for example, by wearing a monitoring device at all times), and comply with directions given by a specified authority in relation to electronic monitoring;
a condition that:
the person carry at all times a specified mobile phone; and
the person be available to answer any call from a specified authority or, as soon as reasonably practicable, return a call that the person was unable to answer; and
the person comply with specified directions, or any directions given by a specified authority, in relation to the condition in subparagraph (i) or (ii);
that the person attend at places, and report to persons, at times, specified:
in the order; or
by a specified authority;

that the person allow visits at specified premises from, and entry to specified premises by, a specified authority at any time for the purpose of ensuring the person’s compliance with a condition imposed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c);
that the person provide a specified authority with a schedule setting out the person’s proposed movements for a specified period and comply with that schedule during the period;
that the person allow any police officer to enter specified premises and:
search the person; and
search the person’s residence or any premises which the person intends to be the person’s residence; and
search any other premises under the person’s control; and
seize any item found during those searches, including to allow the item to be examined forensically;
that the person facilitate access (including by providing passwords or in any other way) to one or more of the following:
electronic equipment or technology;
any data held within, or accessible from, any electronic equipment or technology;
owned or controlled by the person, for the purposes of a police officer searching and seizing any such equipment or accessing such data (or both).
Note 1: For paragraphs (2)(b) and (c), restrictions apply to the use of photographs or impressions of fingerprints (see section 104.5C).
Note 2: For paragraph (2)(d), see also section 104.5D (obligations relating to monitoring devices).

A power exercised under a condition imposed in accordance with subsection (2) (other than a power to give a direction) may be exercised only if the person exercising the power is satisfied that it is reasonably necessary to do so in order to:
give effect to the order; or
facilitate or monitor compliance with the order.
Directions

If a condition imposed on the person by the order authorises a specified authority to give a direction, the specified authority may give a direction only if the specified authority is satisfied that the direction is reasonable in all the circumstances to give effect to:
the condition; or
the object of this Division (see section 104.1).
Limitations
A condition imposed on the person by the order must not require the person to remain at specified premises for more than 12 hours within any 24 hours.

If the person is subject to an order under a law of a State or Territory that is equivalent to a control order, the issuing court must consider the conditions under that State or Territory order in imposing conditions on the person by the order.
General rules about conditions
(7) To avoid doubt, without limiting subsection 33(3A) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, a condition imposed on the person by the order may:
prohibit or restrict specified conduct of the person, or impose obligations on the person; or
impose restrictions and obligations on the person in relation to classes of conduct, and prohibit other classes of that conduct; or
impose different restrictions, obligations and prohibitions in relation to different classes of conduct; or

for conduct that is prohibited by a condition described in a paragraph of subsection (1)—impose restrictions and obligations on the person in relation to that conduct instead of prohibiting that conduct; or
for conduct described in a paragraph of subsection (1) or (2)—impose different restrictions, obligations and prohibitions in relation to that conduct.
Access to lawyers

This section does not affect the person’s right to contact, communicate or associate with the person’s lawyer unless the person’s lawyer is an individual covered by the condition in paragraph (1)(h). If the person’s lawyer is so specified, the person may contact, communicate or associate with any other lawyer who is not so specified.
References to work
In subsection (1), a reference to work includes a reference to voluntary work.
Meaning of premises
In this section:
premises includes a place, an aircraft, a vehicle and a vessel.

section.heading: Conditions where exemptions may be granted

content.p: The issuing court may specify conditions included in the order that are to be exemption conditions.
(2) An exemption condition is a condition specified in the order from which the person may apply for a temporary exemption.
The issuing court may make provision in relation to applications for temporary exemptions.
The person may apply, in writing, to a specified authority for an exemption from an exemption condition. The application must:
include a reason for the exemption; and
comply with any other requirements provided for under subsection (3).
If the person so applies, the specified authority may:
require further information to be provided by the person before making a decision in relation to the application; and
either:
grant or refuse the exemption; or
grant the exemption subject to any reasonable directions specified in writing by the specified authority.

section.heading: Treatment of photographs and impressions of fingerprints

content.p: If the issuing court, by the order, imposes on the person a condition referred to in paragraph 104.5A(2)(b) or (c), a photograph, or an impression of fingerprints, taken of or from the person in accordance with the order must be used only for the purpose of ensuring compliance with the order.
If:
no control order has been in force in relation to the person for 12 months; and
either:
no proceedings relating to a control order relating to the person were on foot in that 12-month period; or
proceedings relating to a control order relating to the person were discontinued or completed within that 12-month period;
the photograph or the impression must be destroyed as soon as practicable after the end of that 12-month period.
A person commits an offence if:
the person engages in conduct; and
the conduct contravenes subsection (1).
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Additional obligations on person
(1) If the issuing court, by the order, imposes on the person the condition referred to in paragraph 104.5A(2)(d) (the monitoring condition) that the person wear a monitoring device, then:
the monitoring condition must require the person to wear the monitoring device at all times; and
the order must include the condition referred to in paragraph 104.5A(2)(e); and
the order must include a condition that the person do all of the following:
allow a specified authority to enter the person’s residence at any reasonable time for any purpose relating to the electronic monitoring of the person;
allow a specified authority to install, repair or fit the monitoring device or any related monitoring equipment;
take the steps specified in the order (if any) and any other reasonable steps to ensure that the monitoring device and any related monitoring equipment are or remain in good working order;
if the person becomes aware that the monitoring device and any related monitoring equipment are not in good working order—notify a specified authority as soon as reasonably practicable;
allow a specified authority, police officer or corrective services officer to remove the monitoring device;
allow a police officer to remove any related monitoring equipment.
Powers of specified authorities and others
After including the monitoring condition in the order, the issuing court must also include in the order an authorisation for:
one or more specified authorities to enter the person’s residence as specified in the order at any reasonable time for any purpose relating to the electronic monitoring of the person; and
one or more specified authorities to install, repair or fit the monitoring device and any related monitoring equipment; and
one or more specified authorities or police officers to take the steps specified in the order to ensure that the device and any related monitoring equipment are or remain in good working order; and
one or more specified authorities, police officers or corrective services officers to remove the monitoring device; and
one or more police officers to remove any related monitoring equipment.
If:
a monitoring device is installed on the person; and
any of the following events occurs:
the monitoring condition is removed from the order;
the order ceases to be in force;
the person is detained in custody;
the device and any related monitoring equipment may be removed in accordance with paragraph (2)(d) or (e) even though no authorisation under subsection (2) is in force.
Note: For the definition of detained in custody, see subsection 100.1(1).
Powers relating to monitoring devices and related electronic equipment
Before exercising a power referred to in paragraph (2)(a), (b), (d) or (e), or subsection (3), a specified authority, police officer or corrective services officer must inform the person:
that the device and equipment are to be installed, repaired, fitted or removed (as the case requires); and
of the proposed timing of the taking of the action; and
that the person may consent to the taking of the action; and
that if consent is not given, reasonable force may be used to take the action, or to enter the person’s residence in order to take the action.
If the person does not give consent, reasonable force may be used by a police officer to take the action, or to enter the person’s residence in order to take the action.

content.p: Insert:
Subdivision EA—Varying a control order by consent
(1) Any of the following persons (the applicant) may apply to the issuing court to vary a control order in relation to a person:
a senior AFP member or a legal representative of the senior AFP member;
the person or a legal representative of the person.
The variation may consist of:
varying or removing one or more of the conditions imposed on the person by the order; or
imposing one or more additional conditions on the person by the order.
The application may be withdrawn at any time before the issuing court decides whether or not to vary the order.

If the person is 14 to 17 years of age, a senior AFP member or a legal representative of the senior AFP member must cause written notice of the application to be given to at least one parent or guardian of the person.
If the person is 14 to 17 years of age, the issuing court may vary the order if the court is satisfied that:
written consent to the variation has been given (and not withdrawn) by:
if the applicant is a senior AFP member or a legal representative of the senior AFP member—a parent or guardian of the person notified of the variation in accordance with subsection (4); or
if the applicant is the person or a legal representative of the person—a senior AFP member; and
the variation is in the best interests of the person, having regard to any representations the person makes about the variation and any other matter the court considers relevant; and
the variation is appropriate in the circumstances.
If the person is 18 years of age or older, the issuing court may vary the order if the court is satisfied that:
written consent to the variation has been given (and not withdrawn) by:
if the applicant is a senior AFP member or a legal representative of the senior AFP member—the person; or
if the applicant is the person or a legal representative of the person—a senior AFP member; and
the variation is appropriate in the circumstances.
If the issuing court varies the order, the varied order must:
state that the court is satisfied of the matters mentioned in subsection (5) or (6) as applicable; and
specify the variations to the conditions that are to be made; and
state the period during which the order, as varied, is in force; and
state that the person’s lawyer may request a copy of the order.

If the issuing court varies the order and the person is 14 to 17 years of age, an AFP member must take reasonable steps to serve a copy of the varied order personally on each parent or guardian of the person notified of the variation in accordance with subsection (4).
